children: The big players in buying exports of U.S. agricultural commodities right now include Canada, Mexico, and China — but none of these markets are expected to grow much from where they are now, says the Farm Journal Foundation in a research note. So to support the increasing output of American farmers, the U.S. will need to nurture relationships with new buyers, says the organization. These new buyers would be in 'emerging markets' such as Africa and South Asia, developing areas that have the potential to expand exponentially and need the food supply to support that expansion. "The U.S. will need to rely on new, potentially rapidly growing markets to build its demand base and protect American farm livelihoods," says the Farm Journal Foundation. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
